floor_history.headline: Recon: floor=9 reconfirmed on pin-free candidate; m2c shows target reconstructs WITHOUT a load-temp (direct inlined stores) and WITHOUT the v1 pointer alias — an untried structural shape; sibling func

Structural sweep (13 forms). Floor held at 9; killed 8 named structural levers; walking-pointer lowers score to 7 but adds an insn so it's architecturally blocked from match — proves the RA tiebreak I
s3 structural sweep lowered pin-free floor 9 -> 6 via mask atomically-first post-call (V7); pre-call proven byte-identical to target so pre-call-freelist hypothesis KILLED.

frontier.hypothesis: Target's exact bytes require load-temp -> $v0 AND mask -> $v1 with mask alive across all three loads. Only a pin (`register mask asm("$3")`) forces the swap in pure C reachable-space. Pure-C RA tiebreak axes measured exhausted this session; any further pin-free progress needs a genuinely novel lever OR canonical-asm authorization for the pin family (siblings func_80061250/func_80061658 share the identical shape).
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2's global.c allocno priority formula log2(refs)*freq*size/live_length gives mask (2 refs, ~7 insn liveness) higher priority than load-temp (6 refs across 3 short webs, or 1 wider web) in the interleaved shape, so mask allocates first to $v0.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/global.c allocno_compare and prioritize_allocno_regs; then dump `-da` .greg for both the pin-free interleaved form (score 9) and target's shape (via cc1psx if it hits 9 too) to see the exact priority ordering. If cc1psx also swaps, the pin family is not pure-C-reachable and canonical-asm authorization is the escape (siblings same shape) -- filing OWNER-ESCALATION becomes justified.

frontier.hypothesis: The V4/V7 score-6 form (mask atomic-first, all-$v0) may be reachable to score 0 by transforming its 6 remaining diffs -- those diffs are scheduling ORDER, not register-renames.
frontier.mechanism: V7 emits all-$v0 but with mask block at top vs target's mask-interleaved; if a structural nudge slotted the mask lui into the load 2 delay slot of the V7 shape (matching target's cycle-2 fill), the mask/load-temp sharing of $v0 might preserve into a byte match.
frontier.next_probe: Directed permuter run seeded from V7 (score 6, all-$v0) rather than V0 (score 9, interleaved-swap) -- PERM_INT_TYPE / PERM_VAR_ORDER around the mask expression; also try (a) mask value written as `0xFF0000 | 0xEF` split across statements, (b) mask via a paired-store to a different global to change the RTL DAG, (c) inserting an inert extra global load whose delay-slot fill target uses.

frontier.hypothesis: Sibling functions func_80061250 (mask=0xFF0060) and func_80061658 (mask=0x10FFFF) share the identical shape and identical $2/$3 pin cheat. A single lever that closes any one closes the family -- so testing V7 (mask-atomic-first) on a sibling and measuring the sibling's score change would triangulate whether V7 is a universal family lever or is specific to 0xFFFFEF's constant shape.
frontier.mechanism: The RA tiebreak is between a 2-insn mask pseudo and a 3x-reused load-temp pseudo. Different 2-insn mask constants (0xFF0060 vs 0xFFFFEF) should have identical priority calc if refs, freq, size, live_length are equal.
frontier.next_probe: Apply V7 shape to func_80061250 or func_80061658 in a scratch sandbox; measure. If both drop 9->6 identically, the family lever exists and lifting the family's remaining 6 diffs closes them all together (worth prioritizing over per-function grind).
